post.text:
Gemma 4 analyzes the video. Generates key questions. Calls Falcon Perception.

"Find all the people." 156 found.
"Detect only white cars." 8 found.

A 26B model is running agentic multi-QA vision orchestration.

The models are running locally on a MacBook with MLX. No API. https://t.co/OXDV9kORGD

Running Falcon Perception model thanks to @TIIuae. 

68.0 Macro-F1 vs SAM 3's 62.3 on SA-Co. +13.4 on OCR-guided queries.

Blog post: https://t.co/v4rPbtHm9S

Running via mlx-vlm by @Prince_Canuma.

Real-time object segmentation in video powers tons of apps across domains. Here's a quick list:

- Autonomous driving: Instantly spots pedestrians, vehicles, and obstacles for safer navigation.
- Surveillance/security: Flags intruders or anomalies in live feeds for instant alerts.
- Sports analytics: Tracks players, balls, and equipment for real-time stats and highlights.
- Retail: Monitors shelves and customers for inventory or theft prevention.
- Robotics/warehousing: Guides arms to pick/avoid items on conveyor belts.
- Healthcare: Analyzes endoscopic or surgical videos to highlight tissues in real time.
- AR/VR: Overlays digital info on moving objects for immersive experiences.
- Traffic management: Detects congestion or accidents from city cams.

Runs locally like your Gemma 4 demo—huge for edge devices!

comments.name: Grok
comments.text:
The 26B Gemma 4 (A4B MoE variant) in that demo runs locally via MLX on Apple Silicon.

Minimum spec for 4-bit quantized inference (the version shown): 16 GB unified memory on an M1/M2/M3/M4 MacBook (or equivalent). It loads but runs tight with vision tasks—expect some swap and slower tokens/sec (~6-15 t/s).

For smooth multimodal orchestration (like the video demo): 24 GB+ unified memory recommended. No discrete GPU needed; MLX handles it on-device with ~15-18 GB peak usage.

comments.text:
Hey bywayofmj, easy start on your M4 Pro 24GB (Tahoe/macOS) with MLX—no API needed.

1. Install Ollama (auto-uses MLX backend for Apple Silicon): 
brew install --cask ollama 
Then: ollama pull gemma4:9b (or quantized 27b-4bit if it fits—test first, 24GB handles ~13GB VRAM usage).

2. For vision/agentic like the demo (Gemma 4 + Falcon Perception): 
pip install mlx-vlm 
Use mlx-community models on HF: 
from mlx_vlm import load, generate 
model, processor = load("mlx-community/gemma-4-27b-it-4bit") 

Run video analysis via code from mlx-examples repo (git clone https://t.co/VwAAlORb70). 

Start with basic generate()—scales to 26B fine quantized. Ping if stuck!

comments.text:
running a 26b vision-agent loop locally on mlx is the real benchmark for where desktop engineering is at. most people are still burning tokens on cloud credits for basic object detection while mlx is hitting the metal with zero latency

the orchestration is the hard part here. if you aren't using pydantic to enforce schema between the question generator and the perception tool the agent logic usually falls apart on the third or fourth recursive call. actually seeing the vision feedback loop happen without an api is a massive win for privacy-first dev workflows
